cf.title: Table sync race with REFRESH PUBLICATION

input.subject: [PATCH] Table sync race with REFRESH PUBLICATION

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated with a reproduction, and the fix re-reads one pg_subscription_rel state under a lock the apply worker already takes, following the sequence-side fix in dca73f7dd03. Confidence is medium because no code was read and only one reviewer has confirmed that the state check is enough without the LSN check.

brief.title: Recheck table sync state under lock after concurrent REFRESH PUBLICATION
brief.problem: An apply worker caches a table's SYNCDONE state, then waits for the subscription lock while ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION removes the table. The worker then tries to mark the missing pg_subscription_rel row READY and errors out, and with disable_on_error the whole subscription is disabled. If two refreshes remove and re-add the table, the old state could skip the new initial copy.
brief.proposed_design: After taking the subscription lock in ProcessSyncingTablesForApply(), the apply worker reads the table's sync state again. It skips origin cleanup and the READY update unless the state is still SYNCDONE, and logs a DEBUG1 message when it skips. v1 also rechecked the sync LSN, but v2 dropped that check after review.
user_visible_surface: New DEBUG1 log message when the apply worker skips the READY transition for a removed or re-added table.
Test patch adds an injection point in tablesync.c before the apply worker locks the subscription.
author_claims: The race disables the whole subscription when disable_on_error = true, including unrelated tables.
An existence-only check is not enough, because a removed and re-added table would skip its new initial copy.
An LLM-assisted review reproduced the missing-row error, and the author tested the remove/re-add case by hand.
There is no field report of the issue that the author knows of.
The table-side issue predates the sequence-side fix in dca73f7dd03.
brief.thread_state: Peter Smith reviewed v1, the author applied his comments in v2, and Peter Smith called 0001 good but asked for more reviewers. The author posted v3 with simpler tests and said the test patch is not meant to be committed.
unclear: The thread does not say which branches are affected or which ones the fix targets for back-patching.
The thread does not show the re-add case being tested in an automated way, and v3 leaves it out of the TAP test.
Only one reviewer has confirmed that the state check alone is safe without the LSN check.
The thread does not say whether the v3 test adds a new injection point that would ship in tablesync.c.

prior_attempts.title: Fix alter subscription concurrency errors
prior_attempts.who_objected: Amit Kapila, Alvaro Herrera, Tom Lane
prior_attempts.quote: I think the patch as-submitted is pretty uninteresting, mainly because the design of adding bespoke lock code for subscription objects doesn't scale.
prior_attempts.reason: Reviewers objected that adding lock-and-retry lookup code specific to subscriptions does not scale, since the same problem affects other object types. Alvaro Herrera suggested using get_object_address() instead, and Tom Lane added that this might first require improving its error reporting. The author did not post an updated version for several commitfests. He then said his own test-flakiness problem had been worked around and that he was not motivated to address the issue for all DDL commands, and the entry was withdrawn.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P3 added new lock-and-retry lookup code for subscription DDL, modeled on dbcommands.c. This proposal adds no lock code: it re-reads one pg_subscription_rel state under the existing lock in the apply worker, following the sequence-side fix in dca73f7dd03.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The fix changes how the logical replication apply worker moves a table from SYNCDONE to READY in tablesync.c.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The apply worker re-reads the pg_subscription_rel state under the subscription lock; the catalog schema does not change.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry targets stable branches, but the thread does not name the affected branches.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: v3-0002 adds an injection point in tablesync.c that would ship if the test patch were committed.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which branches have the race, and which branches does the fix target for back-patching?
When the apply worker skips origin cleanup, does ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION still drop the tablesync origin and slot for the removed table?
Can a re-added table reach SYNCDONE again while the apply worker still waits for the subscription lock, which would make the state check alone insufficient?
Should the remove and re-add case have an automated test, given that it protects against a skipped initial copy?
If the test patch is not committed, what keeps this recheck from being removed by a later change to ProcessSyncingTablesForApply()?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the logical replication tablesync and apply worker code. The visible thread shows one reviewer, Peter Smith, who asked for more reviewers.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the SYNCDONE to READY step on every branch that gets the fix, including that a skipped READY update never leaves a table without its initial copy or an orphaned origin.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 the same day as the review and then v3 with simpler tests, and offered to send more tests on request.

priority.reason: The race needs a REFRESH PUBLICATION at a narrow moment and has no field report, but with disable_on_error it disables the whole subscription. The fix is about 2.4 KB in one file and follows an existing pattern, so a second review by someone who knows tablesync.c is cheap.

provisional_note: No code was read. Two points depend on it: whether the state check alone covers the remove and re-add case, and whether the refresh drops the origin and slot that the apply worker now skips.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Apply worker fails if a relation is missing on subscriber even if refresh publication has not been refreshed yet
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch would let the logical replication apply worker skip changes for tables that were added to a publication but are not yet in pg_subscription_rel on the subscriber, because ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION has not been run. It would log a warning instead of failing repeatedly when such a table is missing on the subscriber.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila questioned whether the current ERROR behavior should be changed when no specific use case had been given. He noted that users can avoid the failure loop with the disable_on_error subscription parameter, and that silently skipping changes could surprise users whose subscriber-side setup is incomplete. The author said he had no specific use case, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I see your point but not sure if it is worth changing the
current behavior without any specific use case which we want to
address with this change.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Reject concurrent sequence refreshes".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Reject concurrent sequence refreshes".
Reverted commit(s): Reject concurrent sequence refreshes.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit f38afa4abb04e85530c94b88daf11c089375daca.

That commit fixed a race that could leave stale sequence values on the
subscriber after 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. It did so by
raising an ERROR during 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'
whenever a sequence synchronization worker was already running for the
subscription.

That approach caused intermittent buildfarm failures, because the existing
tests did not ensure the sequencesync worker had stopped before executing
'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. While discussing how to fix
the tests, we concluded that blocking the command while a sequencesync
worker is running is inconvenient for users. So we will fix the original
race differently in a follow-up commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix alter subscription concurrency errors
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Amit Kapila, Alvaro Herrera, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixed "tuple concurrently updated" errors from concurrent ALTER/DROP SUBSCRIPTION statements on the same subscription by re-fetching the subscription tuple after acquiring its lock, using a retry loop modeled on dbcommands.c. A later version also allowed ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... OWNER TO to run concurrently with the other subscription commands.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers objected that adding lock-and-retry lookup code specific to subscriptions does not scale, since the same problem affects other object types. Alvaro Herrera suggested using get_object_address() instead, and Tom Lane added that this might first require improving its error reporting. The author did not post an updated version for several commitfests. He then said his own test-flakiness problem had been worked around and that he was not motivated to address the issue for all DDL commands, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think the patch as-submitted is pretty uninteresting, mainly because the
design of adding bespoke lock code for subscription objects doesn't scale.

precedents_retrieved.title: tablesync early exit
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes a tablesync worker call process_syncing_tables() before it enters the apply main loop, so a worker with nothing left to do exits early. The author presented it as a small optimization and as a cleaner split of work between tablesync and apply workers.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila objected that exiting before the tablesync worker receives any message skips changes up to the LSN where the copy finished. That is safe with the current code but would lose changes for the table in a design where the apply worker applies streamed in-progress transactions, which had already been proposed on -hackers. The saving was only the work to receive messages for one transaction, so the author withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As per my understanding, this is safe as per the current code but it
can't be guaranteed for future implementations and the amount of extra
work is additional work to receive the messages for one transaction.

precedents_retrieved.title: add subscription TAP test option "vcregress subscriptioncheck" for MSVC builds
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a "subscriptioncheck" option to vcregress.pl so that MSVC builds can run the subscription TAP tests with one command, like "recoverycheck". Later the thread moved to a documentation patch that describes "vcregress taptest" for Windows.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrew Dunstan objected to adding more special targets to vcregress.pl, because the generic taptest option already runs any TAP test set with "vcregress taptest src/test/subscription". The author agreed and switched to a documentation patch. Juan José Santamaría Flecha reviewed that patch and asked for a typo fix and new wording, and the visible messages show no revised version.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I would actually prefer to reduce the number of special things in
vcregress.pl rather than add more.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add statistics refresh materialized view
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add per-view statistics for REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW (execution count and last refresh time) to the statistics collector, exposed as new columns in pg_stat_all_tables and its user/sys variants. The aim was to record when and how often each materialized view was refreshed without relying on pg_stat_statements.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fujii Masao objected that adding columns to pg_stat_all_tables for one utility command is a poor design: it singles out REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW over commands such as TRUNCATE or CLUSTER, would lead to many per-command columns, and the columns would be useless for most entries, which are tables. He also suggested that pg_stat_statements and log_statement could already provide the information per view. The author agreed that these tools may be sufficient for most use cases and withdrew the proposal, and the entry was marked Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's not good design to add new columns per utility command into
pg_stat_all_tables. Otherwise pg_stat_all_tables will have to have lots of
columns to expose the stats of many utility commands at last.

precedents_retrieved.title: EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE on REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, showing the plan of the view's defining SELECT (plain EXPLAIN without refreshing, EXPLAIN ANALYZE performing the refresh), analogous to existing EXPLAIN support for CREATE TABLE AS / CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW. A companion patch refactored ExecRefreshMatView into smaller functions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that supporting EXPLAIN would bind REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW to having an explainable SQL plan, constraining future implementations such as incremental view maintenance, while offering little beyond explaining the view's query directly; the author agreed to withdraw the feature. The leftover refactoring patch was also not taken, because John Naylor judged it would conflict with the refactoring in the pending incremental view maintenance patch without helping it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The problem with it is that it
binds us to the assumption that REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW has an
explainable plan.

precedents_retrieved.title: Subscription code improvements
precedents_retrieved.summary: Petr Jelinek posted a set of logical replication subscription patches: cleaner worker exit messages, a split of SetSubscriptionRelState into separate add and update functions, transactional stopping of workers in ALTER/DROP SUBSCRIPTION, syscache access to pg_subscription without a database connection, and finer-grained subscription locking. Masahiko Sawada later took over the remaining patches for the PG11 cycle.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Part of the set was committed: the transactional worker stop in August 2017, and the message and SetSubscriptionRelState patches in April 2018. The remaining patches, the syscache change and the finer-grained locking, were not committed. Peter Eisentraut found that the locking patch no longer applied and that the syscache patch was of little use without it, and he did not want to review that much code so late. Earlier he had asked what the patches fixed, and the entry had waited on the author since the November commitfest.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: 0004 doesn't apply anymore, 0003 doesn't seem to be very useful without 0004, as I understand it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow granting of permission to REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, CLUSTER, and REINDEX
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, CLUSTER and REINDEX grantable to non-owners, instead of being limited to the table owner, by changing the shared permission check RangeVarCallbackOwnsTable(). The preliminary patch reused the TRUNCATE privilege as a proof of concept; the intended design was a single new table privilege (e.g. REFRESH) covering all three operations.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected to spending one of the four free AclMode privilege bits on this, to reusing TRUNCATE, and to the backward-compatibility effect on existing owner ACLs after upgrade. The discussion then turned to how to extend the privilege-bit space (widening AclMode to 64 bits, a varlena aclitem, or a larger fixed-size aclitem) and whether to use one MAINTAIN privilege or finer-grained ones, without reaching agreement. The CommitFest manager noted no activity over two commitfests and that the thread agreed only that the problem of adding privileges extensibly had to be solved first; after no response, the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So I can't see using one of them up for
REFRESH, let alone using three of them up for REFRESH, CLUSTER and
REINDEX.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent's recorded reason applies. P3 died over new subscription-specific lock code, and this proposal adds none. P2 reverted a fix that raised an error in ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES, while this proposal only skips the READY update in the worker and leaves the user command alone. The thread itself cites dca73f7dd03 as the model (messages #1 and #2), not as an earlier failed attempt.

From the standards and compatibility angle, this bug fix has nothing to object to. It adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or psql change, and dump/restore is not involved; the only user-visible change is a DEBUG1 message, and stopping the subscription from being disabled is the intended result. The thread does not yet name the target back branches, and the v3 test would add an injection point to tablesync.c, but the author says the test is not meant to be committed.

The fix adds a catalog re-read under an existing lock and changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog schema, protocol message or exported API, so back-patching is not blocked by ABI. Not checkable without code: that ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION still drops the tablesync origin and slot when the apply worker skips origin cleanup.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. Only the subscription owner or a superuser can run ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION, and the fix only makes the apply worker skip a catalog update; it adds no new grant, role or default. The DEBUG1 message goes to the server log and names only the relation OID and subscription. The test injection point exists only in builds with injection points enabled.

From the maintenance angle, this is a small recheck of the sync state under a lock the code already takes. It follows the pattern of the sequence-side fix in dca73f7dd03 and adds a catalog read only on the rare SYNCDONE to READY step, so it adds no hot-path cost and no new API, GUC or catalog. [P3] does not apply because the patch adds no new lock code. [P2] concerns blocking a user command and does not apply either. Two committability points remain: no committer has engaged yet, since only Peter Smith reviewed (message #4), and v3-0002 adds an injection point in tablesync.c that would ship if the test patch were committed, although message #5 says it is not meant to be.

This is a bug fix inside the apply worker, and no existing feature, setting or extension can stop the worker from updating a pg_subscription_rel row that is gone. The fix follows the sequence-side recheck in dca73f7dd03 and adds no second mechanism, so item 12 is met, and [P3] (bespoke lock code) does not apply because the patch reuses the existing subscription lock.

This is a small bug fix in tablesync.c, not a feature, so the demand test does not apply in the usual way. The material shows a real failure: a concurrent REFRESH PUBLICATION makes the apply worker error out, disable_on_error then disables the whole subscription, and a re-added table can skip its initial copy. Message #4 confirms the reproduction. The fix adds one catalog read after a lock the worker already takes, so non-users pay almost nothing. The missing field report (messages #1 and #5) weakens the case for the injection-point test, not for the fix.
